followUps.question: What is the difference between a Docker image and a container?
followUps.answer: An image is a read-only template with your app and dependencies. A container is a running instance of that image with its own writable layer.
followUps.interviewPitch: A Docker Image is an immutable, read-only template that contains your source code, libraries, and dependencies. It is essentially the blueprint. A Container is a running instance of that image. You can run hundreds of identical containers from a single image.
followUps.explanation:
**🍰 The Cake Analogy:**
• **Docker Image (The Recipe):** A piece of paper that says 'Add 2 eggs, 1 cup flour, bake at 350'. You can't eat the recipe. It just tells you how to make the cake.
• **Docker Container (The Cake):** The actual, physical cake that you baked using the recipe. You can use the exact same recipe to bake 10 identical cakes (Containers).
followUps.example:
# Build the Recipe (Image)
docker build -t my-app-image .

# Bake the Cake (Container)
docker run -d -p 80:80 my-app-image
followUps.whyAsked: Fundamental Docker concept — confusing images and containers is a red flag.
mistakes: Saying an image is a 'running application' — images are static templates.
Forgetting containers are ephemeral — data is lost without volumes.
followUps.diagram:
flowchart LR
    I[Docker Image (Recipe)] -->|docker run| C1[Container 1]
    I -->|docker run| C2[Container 2]
    I -->|docker run| C3[Container 3]

followUps.question: What is Docker Compose and when do you use it?
followUps.answer: Docker containers share the host OS kernel and isolate at the process level. VMs run a full guest OS on a hypervisor, providing hardware-level isolation.
followUps.interviewPitch: Docker Compose is a tool for defining and running multi-container Docker applications. Instead of running 5 massive `docker run` commands in the terminal with complex network flags, you write a single `docker-compose.yml` file. I use it exclusively for local development to spin up my Web API, SQL Server, and Redis cache all at the exact same time with a single command.
followUps.explanation:
**🎼 The Sheet Music Analogy:**
If you have a drummer, a guitarist, and a singer (3 Containers), you don't want to walk up to each of them individually and tell them what to play and how loud to play it.

Docker Compose is the **Sheet Music**. You write down all the rules for the entire band on one piece of paper. You hand it out, wave your baton (`docker-compose up`), and the entire band starts playing together in perfect harmony.
followUps.example:
# ✅ docker-compose.yml
version: '3.8'
services:
  web:
    image: my-web-api
    ports:
      - "8080:80"
  db:
    image: mcr.microsoft.com/mssql/server
    environment:
      SA_PASSWORD: "SuperSecret123!"
followUps.whyAsked: Tests understanding of virtualization levels — critical for cloud architecture decisions.
mistakes: Saying Docker replaces VMs — they solve different problems and often coexist.
Claiming containers have no security isolation — namespaces + cgroups provide strong isolation.
followUps.diagram:
flowchart TD
    DC[docker-compose up] --> API[Web API Container]
    DC --> DB[SQL Server Container]
    DC --> Redis[Redis Container]
    Note over API, DB: All connected to the same virtual network!
